steps.description:
Your lab needs to simulate how a particular cell spreads over time in a linear space. A sample space below shows a single cell 1 (0 indicates no cell). 0 0 1 0 0 0 0

Everyday, a cell will spread to its adjacent neighbours (left and right). You need to count how many days it takes for the space to be completely filled with cells. An example below takes 4 days. Day 0: 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 Day 1: 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 Day 2: 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 Day 3: 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Day 4: 1 1 1 1 1 1 1

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input the length of the space. 2. Ask user to input the index position of a cell in the space. 3. Call a function to display the day number starting from 0 and the space. 4. Call a function to update the spread of the cells in 1 day. 5. Repeat step (3) to (4) for until the whole space is filled with live cells. 6. Display the total number of days taken.

You'll need to create 2 functions: one function for display and one function for updating the spread. Decide what arguments to pass to the functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

You can try this for fun: If you modify your display function to clear the screen before display each day and delay for 1 second, you will see a cool animation! To clear the screen in replit, you can do the following: import replit replit.clear()

Test Input

5 4

8 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter space size: 5 Enter cell position: 4 Day 0: 0 0 0 0 1 Day 1: 0 0 0 1 1 Day 2: 0 0 1 1 1 Day 3: 0 1 1 1 1 Day 4: 1 1 1 1 1 Total 4 days

Example 2 Enter space size: 8 Enter cell position: 2 Day 0: 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 0 Day 1: 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 0 Day 2: 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 0 Day 3: 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 Day 4: 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Day 5: 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 Total 5 days

Your lab needs to simulate how a particular cell spreads over time in a 2D grid space. A sample grid space below shows a single cell 1 in the grid (0 indicates no cell).      Every day, a cell will spread to its adjacent neighbours (left, right, up and down). You need to count how many days it takes for the grid to be completely filled with cells. The example below takes 3 days. Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input the size of the grid in row and column. 2. Ask user to input the position of a cell in row index and column index. 3. Call a function to display the day number starting from 0 and the grid. 4. Call a function to update the spread of the cells in 1 day. 5. Repeat steps (3) to (4) for until the whole grid is filled with live cells. 6. Display the total number of days taken.

You'll need to create 2 functions: one function for display and one function for updating the spread. Decide what arguments to pass to the functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - Updating a list while using it for checking may cause a problem. - The following command deepcopy() using copy library for duplicating a 2D list may be useful: import copy copy_mylist = copy.deepcopy(mylist)

You can try this for fun: If you modify your display function to clear the screen before displaying each day and delay for 1 second, you will see a cool animation! To clear the screen in replit, you can do the following: import replit replit.clear()

Test Input

2 4 1 3

4 5 2 1

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter grid size (row column): 2 4 Enter cell position (row column): 1 3 Total 4 days

Example 2 Enter grid size (row column): 4 5 Enter cell position (row column): 2 1

Total 5 days
